chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Khaḍir al-Ṣayrafī, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah al-ʿIjlī, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a man who intentionally killed another man, but the prescribed punishment was not carried out against him and the testimony was not established until he became mentally disturbed and lost his intellect. Then some other people testified against him after he had become mentally disturbed that he had killed him. He said: “If they testify against him that he killed at the time he killed while he was sound and had no defect from corruption of intellect, he is to be killed for it. But if they do not testify against him to that, and he has known property, the blood money is to be given to the heirs of the slain from the property of the killer. And if he did not leave any property, the blood money is to be given from the public treasury, and the blood of a Muslim person is not to be left uncompensated.”
Al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام:

“Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام asking him about an insane man who intentionally killed a man. So he placed the blood money upon his people, and he made his intentional act and his mistake the same.”

key_terms.اَلدِّيَةُ: blood money owed as legal compensation for killing
key_terms.بَيْتِ اَلْمَالِ: the public treasury from which compensation may be paid
key_terms.خُولِطَ: he became mentally disturbed or confused in mind
key_terms.مَجْنُونٍ: an insane person lacking sound intellect

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a murderer becomes insane before the testimony is established?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out rulings concerning homicide when the killer loses mental capacity after the act. If witnesses establish that the killing occurred while he was mentally sound, retribution applies; otherwise, blood money is paid from his property or from the public treasury so that the blood of a Muslim is not left without due compensation.
